concepts.learning_objective: Describe the political and economic features of the Soviet system that came up after the 1917 revolution.
Explain how the east European countries formed the Second World or socialist bloc led by the USSR.
Identify the bureaucratic, authoritarian and national weaknesses of the Soviet system.
Explain why Gorbachev introduced reforms and what perestroika and glasnost meant.
Trace the sequence of events from 1985 to December 1991 that ended the Soviet Union.
Describe how Russia became the successor state of the Soviet Union and how the CIS was formed.

topics.title: Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how military spending, satellite states and shortages led to Soviet economic stagnation.
Analyse how an unaccountable party and stifling administration alienated Soviet citizens.
Evaluate the rise of nationalism in the republics as the most immediate cause of the collapse.
Explain why the collapse of the Soviet bloc ended Cold War confrontations and the arms race.
Analyse the change in power relations that made the US the sole superpower.
Describe the aspirations of the new countries that emerged from the Soviet bloc.
Identify the main features of the shock therapy model of transition to capitalism.
Explain the economic and social consequences of shock therapy in Russia and the region.
Evaluate the state of democratic institutions and the economic revival in post-Soviet states.
Identify the secessionist movements and civil wars in the former Soviet republics.
Explain why Central Asia became a zone of competition between outside powers.
Compare the peaceful split of Czechoslovakia with the violent break-up of Yugoslavia.
Describe the economic, political, military and cultural ties between India and the USSR during the Cold War.
Explain the shared multipolar vision of India and Russia and the benefits each gains from the relationship.
Interpret the popularity of Indian films and culture in post-Soviet countries.
